Albion Online doesn't have traditional fast travel the way most MMOs do, but here's what you can actually use:

**Travel Planner NPC** — this is the closest thing to fast travel between major cities. It's found northeast of the central plaza in every city, marked by a yellow compass icon. It allows instant travel between cities and islands on the Royal Continent, and to/from hideouts and small towns in the Outlands.

The catch: it never allows you to transport tradable items when traveling to or from Caerleon, hideouts, or Outland towns. Basically, you're traveling light or you're not fast traveling.

**If you're out in the world gathering** — there's no fast travel back to town from yellow or blue zones. You walk. Use a transport mount and pork pie to make the haul easier.

**Between cities on foot** — follow the yellow roads on the map to neighboring clusters, finding the shortest route with the fewest zones between you and your destination. Avoid red and black zones if you don't want to risk PvP.

So short version: if you're already in a city and want to jump to another city with no inventory, use the Travel Planner NPC (compass icon, northeast of the central plaza). If you've got loot on you, you're walking or mounting up.

Albion Online is entering a new era with its next major update, Radiant Wilds. Launching on April 13, this update refreshes and strengthens the game's foundations. From a sweeping visual upgrade to smarter tools and performance improvements, this update breathes new life into the game’s core systems while adding new ways to explore, experiment, and fight. At the heart of the update is a visual overhaul of the open world. Each of Albion’s biomes have been refreshed with improved lighting, updated vegetation, enhanced ground textures, and new water graphics. Stronger color grading, cloud shadows, and biome-specific environmental effects make each region feel more alive, all while preserving the distinctive visual style that defines Albion. Radiant Wilds also introduces major technical and performance improvements, as extensive work behind the scenes improves the overall health of the game client.

Together, these changes mark the beginning of Albion’s next chapter, strengthening its foundations while opening the door to everything that comes next. Welcome to a radiant new era! Radiant Wilds refreshes Albion’s open world with a wide-ranging visual upgrade. Improved textures and lighting make traveling through Albion a truly immersive, vivid experience, with brighter sunlight, more vibrant colors, and water that feels lifelike and reflective of its surroundings. Each biome’s characteristic look and feel has been enhanced. Ground textures feel more varied, from boggy swamps to dusty steppes, while surfaces glitter with snow, sand, and water reflecting the light. New vegetation has been added alongside atmospheric details like insects in the undergrowth and snow borne by sudden gusts of wind. The sky also feels more dynamic, with passing clouds reflected on the ground and in the water as it flows past.

Journey Back still exists as of the current patch notes — it hasn't been removed. So the issue is more likely one of these:

**Most probable causes for why you can't find it:**

1. **You're in the Royal Continent** — Journey Back only works from the Outlands and black zones. If you're in yellow/blue zones on the Royal Continent, the button flat out won't appear or won't be usable.

2. **It's a mount ability** — it's not a standalone UI button. It lives in your mount's skill bar. You need to be **mounted** to see and use it. If you're on foot, it won't be there.

3. **Zone restriction** — entering a Smuggler's Den resets active Journey Back bindings, so if you've been in one of those recently it may have cleared it.

4. **Disarray** — if you're in a large group, Disarray debuff blocks the ability entirely.

So practically: get on your mount while you're out in the Outlands or a black zone, then look at your mount ability bar. The Journey Back button should be there. If you're on the Royal Continent gathering in yellow zones, there's no equivalent — you walk back.

content.text: where are combat mounts useful?

chat_messages.text:
Combat mounts have mounted abilities specifically designed for fighting — things like charges, knockbacks, or damage boosts — so they're useful anywhere you're likely to get into PvP while still needing mobility. The main scenarios:

**Open world PvP** — ganking or escaping gankers in red/black zones, where having a mount that can fight rather than just flee gives you an edge.

**Large-scale battles** — some combat mounts like the Direwolf or Swamp Dragon are used in ZvZ (zerg vs zerg) for their AoE or CC abilities before you dismount into the fight.

**Roaming small-group PvP** — when you're hunting in the Outlands with a small group and expect to engage, a combat mount lets you contribute before the dismount.

**Faction Warfare** — mounted combat has become more relevant there since Realm Divided reworked the system, and combat mounts give you tools beyond just running flags.

They're generally not useful for PvE, gathering, or transport — for those you want speed mounts or ox/transport mounts respectively. The tradeoff is that combat mounts are usually slower than pure speed mounts and carry less weight than transport mounts, so you're sacrificing utility for the mounted fighting capability.
